description: Fleet session-management Phase B, D1 (§4). The lane-landing verb: composes FOUR steps in fixed order, each idempotent, with no cross-table transaction — (1) terminate_session, which invokes the existing host driver (headless workers: SIGTERM then SIGKILL after grace; operator-hosted rows: no host action by design, reported as host_action 'none_available') BEFORE the ledger write, and tolerates an already-terminal row; (2) prune this session's session_role_claim cardinality row if one still names a role bound to it (best-effort cleanup, not role_binding release itself); (3) fire every armed session_terminal dependency edge waiting on this agent_instance_id, guarded by fired_at IS NULL so a re-run never double-fires; (4) a predicated ledger write terminated -> retired. Before step (1) a derivable lane worktree is adjudicated: every uncommitted or untracked path needs an exact recoverable copy (its raw bytes, Git mode and kind, or its absence) in the integration head's tree or, for the session's own registered Unit, in a landing commit reachable from that head, a frozen candidate whose packet or retained commit still holds those bytes, or a registered document whose full bytes read back and verify; declared build output and empty directories hold no bytes. Unique bytes refuse with lane_worktree_not_disposable before the host is touched. After termination, removal re-adjudicates against the current files and freshly read evidence and retains the worktree (worktree_disposition retained_not_disposable) if anything changed; the lane branch is never deleted or moved. Register evidence that cannot be read or verified is an advisory: locally provable disposal still passes and unproven bytes stay protected. A crash mid-retire leaves the row 'terminated'-but-not-'retired'; re-running retire_session on the same agent_instance_id skips completed steps and drives it home — re-drivable by construction, never wedged. host_action describes THIS call: terminated means driver invocation returned, none_available means no supported action, not_attempted means no new invocation. host_remedy describes this call. prior_host_outcome is the latest versioned terminated-transition attempt (also present after the first successful attempt), including action, remedy, observation, exact agent_instance_id/host/host_ref, observed_at, provenance and transition_id; null means unknown. prior_host_reason preserves the raw append-only rationale, and prior_host_advisory names missing, malformed or unreadable evidence. host_liveness is alive/dead/unknown from a fresh exact native probe; host_liveness_detail and host_liveness_observed_at describe it. registry_checked distinguishes an absent registry from a checked-absent binding; peer_registration is the independently read remaining binding or null. teardown_complete is true only for observed dead AND registry checked absent. not_done lists unresolved host and registration facts. completed describes the transport/ledger operation, not proof of host teardown. A caller may pin one immutable custody packet for this call only, with unit_id, repository_id and assignment_sha256 matching the managed row and the spawning coordinator's current binding, exactly as preserve_lane_evidence requires: packet_id names an existing packet, or preserve_evidence=true with disposition, rationale and optional predecessor_packet_id captures and read-verifies one through preserve_lane_evidence first; both need expected_fingerprint, and naming both is refused as ambiguous. A pinned packet replaces register custody: before termination and again immediately before removal the packet is reverified as a whole and a complete current inventory of the lane, staged entries, stages and flags included, must refingerprint to exactly that fingerprint, even where local custody alone would pass. Any corrupt, missing, foreign, stale or changed packet or lane refuses before the host is touched, or after termination retains the worktree, and never falls back to local custody; unsupported index state or protected leaves are named as incomplete custody and stay in place. Nothing is recaptured after consent, a superseded disposition never retires bytes without verified custody, the packet stays readable by read_lane_evidence after removal, and no packet is pruned or withdrawn. Omitting the packet selects nothing for that call, so sweeps, spawn rollback, canaries and default callers are unchanged. A pinned packet remains explicit and call-scoped. The packet must have been captured from the still-extant bound original through preserve_lane_evidence; a manually copied directory or its hashes are not native custody and cannot be imported as a packet. Keep any external Controller copy intact. This workflow does not recover bytes after the original lane is absent. Packet recovery proves bytes only, not landing, host death or deletion authority.
embedding_description: Retire a managed session with authorized host, ledger and worktree steps via retire_session. For unique bytes, capture the still-extant bound original using preserve_lane_evidence, then select its packet by id and fingerprint; preserve_evidence captures in one request. Manual copies and hashes are not native custody; retain external copies. Packets prove bytes, not landing or host death.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: already_retired and dependencies_fired describe this call. host_action describes THIS call: terminated means driver invocation returned, none_available means no supported action, not_attempted means no new invocation. host_remedy describes this call. prior_host_outcome is the latest versioned terminated-transition attempt (also present after the first successful attempt), including action, remedy, observation, exact agent_instance_id/host/host_ref, observed_at, provenance and transition_id; null means unknown. prior_host_reason preserves the raw append-only rationale, and prior_host_advisory names missing, malformed or unreadable evidence. host_liveness is alive/dead/unknown from a fresh exact native probe; host_liveness_detail and host_liveness_observed_at describe it. registry_checked distinguishes an absent registry from a checked-absent binding; peer_registration is the independently read remaining binding or null. teardown_complete is true only for observed dead AND registry checked absent. not_done lists unresolved host and registration facts. completed describes the transport/ledger operation, not proof of host teardown. custody_packet is present only for a pinned packet and retains packet_id, fingerprint, captured and worktree_disposition unchanged.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Read teardown_complete and not_done before describing the result. A repeat can report not_attempted while preserving a prior none_available remedy and an unresolved host gap. A missing historical envelope is unknown, not success. Never infer death from completed, a terminal ledger state, driver return or absent peer registration. Quote operator manual remedies. A custody packet proves recoverable bytes, not landing or host death; report its id and retained/removed disposition. No role eviction, live-host deregistration or new host capability is introduced.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Composes terminate_session's predicated transition, a best-effort session_role_claim prune, a guarded dependency-edge fire, and a final predicated terminated->retired write. No step spans a transaction with another; each is individually idempotent so a partial failure is safely re-drivable by calling this verb again with the same agent_instance_id. A pinned packet may be an existing packet_id with expected_fingerprint, or one captured in this request with preserve_evidence=true, expected_fingerprint, disposition, rationale and an optional predecessor_packet_id. Capture uses preserve_lane_evidence against the still-extant bound original and reads the new packet back before retirement proceeds. A manual copy or hash is not native custody; external copies remain untouched. Packet recovery proves bytes only, not landing, host death or deletion authority.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: session_not_found: no managed_session row exists for the given agent_instance_id. stale_lifecycle_state: the final terminated->retired write lost a race with another writer between this call's read and its write (rare — nothing else legitimately writes a terminated row's state except this verb). lane_worktree_not_disposable: the lane worktree still holds bytes with no exact recoverable copy; the message names each such path and every custody advisory, such as a register read that failed, a candidate that is not frozen or names another Unit, or a landing commit not reachable from master. lane_worktree_adjudication_failed: Git could not read the lane worktree, so nothing was decided. custody_selection_ambiguous: both packet_id and preserve_evidence or capture fields were given. custody_selection_invalid: a pinned packet lacks expected_fingerprint, a capture lacks disposition or rationale, or capture fields came without packet_id or preserve_evidence. custody_identity_mismatch or coordinator_authority_denied: the request is not the managed row's own Unit or the caller is not its coordinator. custody_incomplete, custody_fingerprint_stale or custody_publication_failed from a capture, and a lane_worktree_not_disposable message naming a custody_ code, mean the pinned packet did not hold the lane; no host was terminated.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For lane_worktree_not_disposable, preserve the named paths by delivering the candidate or registering the exact document, then re-request retirement; never delete them to pass the check. For a pinned-packet refusal, while the original managed lane still exists, call preserve_lane_evidence using its bound identity and a fresh read_lane_evidence snapshot fingerprint, with disposition and rationale. Then call retire_session with that explicit packet_id and fingerprint, or use the one-call preserve_evidence form with the same required fingerprint, disposition and rationale. Retirement re-verifies the packet and fresh complete lane inventory before host action and before removal. Manual copies and hashes are not native custody; retain any external copy. If the original is absent, this workflow does not recover it. A packet proves recoverable bytes only, not landing, host death or deletion authority.
